In detail

Residential Tallinn, and the review found nothing area-specific for it in Estonian sources — not in ERR's or Postimees's crime reporting, and not among the districts the city names in its prevention work. Estonia publishes national crime statistics rather than a geolocated neighbourhood dataset, so this is genuinely an absence of findings: the dashed outline says the ground was not examined, not that it was checked and cleared.

Frequently asked questions

Is Haabersti safe?

Wandroz rates Haabersti in Tallinn as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Tallinn. That rating rests on an area-level review that reached no traveller-relevant reporting specific to Haabersti — no incidents, no recurring problems, nothing documented either way — read together with the character of the area. It is not a positive finding of safety: an absence of reporting is weaker evidence than the sourced ratings elsewhere on this map, and it is marked as such wherever it appears.

What was checked for Haabersti?

The same area-level review every other neighbourhood on the Tallinn map gets: local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist, searched for this specific area. Haabersti returned nothing traveller-relevant, which is common for smaller administrative areas without a press profile of their own. Where a review does return something, the sources are named on the area's page.

Is Haabersti a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it. For a stay, weigh that against the areas on the Tallinn map whose ratings are backed by named sources, and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
